Maya Chen: FYI draft for a customer-facing note — ACME (Dedicated / Private) had a GPU card with recurring ECC/Xid alerts. proposing a short notice about draining and card replacement. please review :wave:
Arjun Patel: paste draft when ready, I'll check the technical bits.
Maya Chen: Draft (please review/edit):
---
Hello ACME team,

We're reaching out about a hardware issue detected on one of the GPUs in your Dedicated cluster (eu-west-1, node: gpu-12). Starting 2026-06-18 02:12 UTC our monitoring observed repeated ECC and Xid errors on GPU 0. To prevent intermittent failures we will proactively drain the GPU and replace the card.

What to expect:
- Routing: Instances on gpu-12 will be drained and workloads will be routed to redundant capacity within your Dedicated pool. We expect failover to be automatic with minimal impact to ongoing requests.
- Duration: The drain+replacement work is estimated to take up to 2 hours from start of maintenance, but failover and normal traffic routing should complete within 1-5 minutes for most requests.
- Impact: Customers using pinned capacity may see temporary throttling if you are at committed utilization; otherwise no interruption for standard burst-backed workloads. There may be a small number of requests that experience retries or 5xx errors during the drain window — our system will retry and route where possible.
- Follow-up: We'll post a completion notice with timestamps and the replaced card's serial.

If you have constraints for a maintenance window or require us to wait, reply and we'll coordinate. For high-SLA flows we can schedule a formal maintenance window.

Best,
Redwood Inference — Customer Success
---

Zoe Li: This is good. Two notes: 1) remove the exact node name `gpu-12` in the public-facing line, keep it in the internal details. 2) add a short troubleshooting list customers can do (e.g., reduce pinned throughput or switch to fallback model).
Maya Chen: updated draft with those changes: kept node in internal only, added suggestions for customers.
Arjun Patel: Technical accuracy check: mention ECC/Xid but avoid implying software bug. Suggest: "hardware-level memory errors (ECC) triggered Xid GPU exceptions; diagnostics indicate degraded memory module on one card." Also add that KV-cache for chat sessions is preserved and will be replayed where possible.
Mateo Ramos: Add capacity note: "We have a hot-spare pool in eu-west-1 but it's shared across a few Dedicated customers; if utilization is high we may shift to nearest region fallback — we'll notify if cross-region routing required."
Maya Chen: incorporated Arjun and Mateo edits. New draft below (final candidate):
---
Hello ACME team,

We're writing to notify you of a proactive hardware maintenance event in your Dedicated deployment. On 2026-06-18 02:12 UTC our monitoring detected repeated hardware-level memory errors (ECC) which triggered GPU Xid exceptions on one card serving your cluster. Diagnostics indicate a degraded memory module and we plan to replace the card to prevent intermittent failures.

What to expect:
- Failover behavior: Traffic will be routed to redundant capacity in your Dedicated pool. Most requests will failover automatically within 1-5 minutes.
- Maintenance duration: The full drain and hardware swap may take up to 2 hours; normal traffic routing should complete much sooner.
- Potential impact: If your Dedicated pool is at committed capacity we may apply short throttling while we rebalance. For burst-enabled workloads we expect no visible interruption. A small number of in-flight requests may return transient 5xx errors; our frontends will retry where safe.
- KV cache: Session context held in KV-cache is preserved and replayed where possible; long-running generation may restart and continue from the last cached state.
- Cross-region fallback: We have hot-spare capacity in eu-west-1; if the spare capacity is saturated we may route to the nearest compatible region and will notify you if that occurs.

If you need this to occur during a specific maintenance window, or you want us to delay the replacement, reply to this thread and we'll coordinate.

We'll post a completion update with timestamps and the replaced card's serial number once the work is done.

Best,
Redwood Inference — Customer Success
---
